catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds the four normalized body-rate components of the upstream geometry_msgs/Twist. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires linear_velocity in m/s, angular_velocity in rad/s and a duration_s, while the clone states no physical unit or bounded duration for cmd_vel; the internal controller clamps its own output to -1..1 but the topic consumer's envelope is outside the clone.

No catalogue class binds a no-input mission-start publication. cap.device.configure.v1 is a writable state patch, while /start_mission is an effectful std_msgs/Empty publication whose callback only sets mission_ true.

No catalogue class binds a transmission-only mission stop. cap.motion.stop.v1 requires a deceleration in m/s2 and reports a stopping position; the clone's /stop_mission is an unacknowledged Empty publication that publishes a zero Twist and may forward a land action, so binding the catalogue class would invent deceleration and stopped-state evidence.

G1 pass, G2 pass, G3 fail (G3.STRICT SAFE-045: an R2 hardware device needs an independent hardware e-stop or a non-empty safe_state.achieved_by; G3.NO_ESTOP: no native stop), G4 pass, G5/G6/G8/G9 NOT_RUN, G7 warn G7.ROS_NO_MESSAGES. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was emitted. The report of this run is check-report.json; it was not hand-edited.

WHY THERE IS NO SAFE PATH: the launched controller is drone_base (launch/launch_one.py:28-33), not the Python entry symbol. drone_base subscribes to /stop_mission (src/drone_base.cpp:181) and its callback calls stop_mission() (src/drone_base.cpp:259-264), which clears mission_, calls all_stop() (src/drone_base.cpp:266-273) and, only when the state is flight or flight_odom, calls start_action(Action::land). all_stop publishes a zero velocity (src/drone_base.cpp:428-432). start_action drops the action when the action manager is busy (src/drone_base.cpp:381-396); otherwise it sends a TelloAction request to the external tello_action service (src/action_mgr.cpp:8-21). The service response rc==OK only marks acceptance and leaves the manager waiting; completion arrives later on the tello_response topic (src/action_mgr.cpp:23-48,50-70; include/action_mgr.hpp:11-20). A topic publication and a zero Twist are not acknowledged stop bindings, and the clone contains no ROS service or action server that stops the drone. The Python flyer's stop explicitly does not try to land (src/flock_simple_path.py:202-215), and no shipped launch starts that script. Adding a safe_state=True action over a publication is rejected by the RosBridge, so the package declares no e-stop binding and no safe-state action instead of claiming a stop the source cannot establish.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the Python entry symbol flock_simple_path:TrajectoryVelocityFlyer (src/flock_simple_path.py:175) and the family:ros/RosDriver helper. The symbol exists and is installed (CMakeLists.txt:129-130), but it is a demo helper rather than a launched ROS service. This package is a configuration-only RosDriver over the production drone_base topic contract; it does not import or start the Python code. A direct Driver over the helper would not supply a safe stop either, because the helper's only stop path is the zero-velocity call above.

COVERED on the fake backend only: /start_mission, /stop_mission and /solo/cmd_vel publications, and three /solo/base_odom reads (pose position, pose orientation, twist). The shipped single-drone launch runs drone_base under namespace solo (launch/launch_one.py:31-33), so the relative cmd_vel and base_odom endpoints are declared at /solo/...; a different deployment namespace requires remapping. The four cmd_vel components are declared as normalized rate components because the clone states no physical unit; every numeric input is Limit.operator_required, so hardware calls are refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator supplies site-limits.json. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative overlay with example values, not device facts. The fake is a ROS-free in-memory contract stand-in, not a recording and not the upstream simulator; every number in it is marked '# placeholder'. NOT COVERED: the /plan input, takeoff/land commands, the joystick path, the external tello_action and tello_response contract, camera or image output (flock2 exposes none), and any physical stop, landing or flight-dynamics claim. No hardware was attached, no hardware backend or ROS graph was run, no human reviewed or tested anything, and driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null. The loader refuses the hardware backend of this model-authored R2 package until a human signs that review; fake evidence is contract_checked only and is not a hardware run.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the launched drone_base (launch/launch_one.py:31-33, namespace solo) subscribes to /stop_mission (src/drone_base.cpp:181), whose callback clears the mission flag, publishes a zero velocity (all_stop, 428-432) and only in flight states asks for a land action (266-274) that start_action drops when the action manager is busy (381-396); the TelloAction service response only marks acceptance and completion arrives later on tello_response (src/action_mgr.cpp:23-72), and no ROS service or action server in the clone stops the drone. A publication, a zero Twist and a LAND request are not an acknowledged stop, so the R2 hardware package declares no stop and G3 fails SAFE-045 and NO_ESTOP, which is the honest outcome. The four topic bindings (/solo/cmd_vel, /start_mission, /stop_mission, /solo/base_odom with pose.pose and twist.twist paths) match their lines, every cmd_vel input is operator_required with an example overlay, and the R1-to-R2 raise for a flying drone is right. Two imprecisions remain for the next author: the fact citing src/action_mgr.cpp:50-70 says an action ends only on a tello_response message, but spin_once also fails it from the initial service response (35-44); the fact citing launch/launch_one.py:28-33 says the launch does not start flock_simple_path, an absence those six lines cannot show. Two further defects for the next author (coordinator patterns 2 and 3): the three /solo/base_odom bindings are automatic resource reads, but nothing in the clone publishes base_odom for the shipped launch (it comes from the external visual localizer, only while fiducials are seen), and a probe with that topic silent (review/lists/r03-probe_silent_flock2_timing.py) showed every command waiting for the snapshot: the protective /stop_mission publication left only after 1.0 s and its receipt after 2.0 s, which the always-answering fake hides; the observations should be explicit read capabilities. The shipped launch also starts competing publishers on the bound topics: drone_base publishes /solo/cmd_vel itself (src/drone_base.cpp:313-315, 431) and flock_base publishes /start_mission and /stop_mission from joystick buttons (src/flock_base.cpp:27-28, 47-50). The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings (stable digest sha256:92384d7973c16fcecdd017bc4a318ed65313fb103db4493f2db867be762439b1; RESULT.json records the superseded run's report_digest). For the human reviewer: Ryze Tello quadcopters through tello_driver (outside the clone): /solo/cmd_vel drives the drone directly and competes with drone_base's own cmd_vel publisher, and flock_base can publish /start_mission and /stop_mission from the joystick; /stop_mission zeroes the velocity and may request a land that can be dropped while another action is busy, and in this package it waits up to 1 s behind a silent /solo/base_odom snapshot before it is even published. Unblocking needs a physical kill path (the Tello has none the clone exposes) or an acknowledged stop the SDK can bind; LAND and the zero Twist do not certify safety.
